nodes.label: build.yml Release Artifact Pipeline
macOS arm64 .dmg — the one SUPPORTED release artifact
macOS code-signing intentionally OFF (APPLE_* env vars omitted, not blanked)
nodes.rationale: A missing GitHub secret expands to an empty string; if APPLE_CERTIFICATE were set to "" the bundler would treat it as Some("") and fail importing an empty keychain blob. Leaving the env vars unset entirely makes env::var(...).ok() return None so tauri-bundler skips signing cleanly and emits an unsigned .dmg, matching the loops.md P2 decision that signing is not yet configured.

nodes.label: tauri-apps/tauri-action build+release step
Basic CI — Release Gate A (fmt · clippy · test · build on macOS)
Alpha CI runs one supported OS (macOS) instead of a 3-OS matrix
nodes.rationale: macOS is the alpha's primary development and target platform; broadening to macOS/Linux/Windows is deferred to the P3 backlog item in .loopdeck/loops.md and lands after the cross-boundary OS distribution contract is signed.

nodes.label: ci.yml supersedes the old rust.yml workflow
nodes.rationale: rust.yml only ran ubuntu build+test; ci.yml covers that plus fmt, clippy, and the frontend build in one macOS job.

loopdeck project.yaml metadata
AGENTS.md — LoopDeck project conventions (.Codex variant)
CLAUDE.md — LoopDeck project conventions (.claude variant)
README — LoopDeck product overview

SECURITY.md — agent/subprocess threat model
T1 — Subprocess/PATH hijack from an imported project
nodes.rationale: A malicious project could ship a claude/git script and rely on $PATH resolution (a . or empty entry) to execute under LoopDeck's privileges; mitigated by resolving both binaries to absolute, vetted, OnceLock-pinned paths before spawn.

nodes.label: T2 — Destructive or undesired agent action (incl. prompt injection)
nodes.rationale: A buggy or prompt-injected agent may attempt destructive commands or unwanted edits; mitigated by --permission-mode default plus the four-arm answer_control_request flow (AskUserQuestion, destructive floor, manual-approval interception, ConfirmChanges fallback).

nodes.label: T3 — Path traversal / symlink escape at the IPC boundary
nodes.rationale: Project-scoped IPC commands could be fed paths that escape the registered root or follow a planted symlink; mitigated by the paths module's canonical_root/resolve_registered_root/resolve_within containment helpers.

nodes.label: T4 — Unbounded-input DoS / memory exhaustion
nodes.rationale: A huge scan tree, pathological transcript line, or runaway response accumulation could freeze the UI; mitigated by the limits module's depth/entry/time/byte budgets across scan, search, file-read, and streaming paths.

nodes.label: T5 — Agent auth token exposure
nodes.rationale: The model-provider key must not leak into backups, logs, or the renderer. Current mitigation stores it in an owner-only 0600 agent_token file separate from config.yaml, injected into the child env only at spawn time. This supersedes the earlier 2026-07-10 decision to store it in the macOS Keychain, which was reverted because unsigned builds re-prompted for the keychain password on every spawn.

nodes.label: T6 — Corrupted or crash-inconsistent state
nodes.rationale: A crash mid-write could truncate the registry; mitigated by persist::atomic_write (temp-file + fsync + rename) plus a .bak sibling and 4-step recovery that never silently overwrites a malformed primary.

nodes.label: T7 — Unsigned / un-notarized build provenance
nodes.rationale: macOS cannot cryptographically verify the binary's provenance; notarization is deferred for recurring Apple Developer Program cost, so the operator must explicitly bypass Gatekeeper on install.

nodes.label: Prompt injection is inherent — LoopDeck mitigates actions, not reasoning
Use Tauri v2 for desktop shell
nodes.rationale: Electron's bundle size and the need for a performant filesystem scanner pushed evaluation toward Tauri; chosen for smaller bundle and better FS performance at the cost of maintaining Rust + TypeScript across the IPC boundary.

nodes.label: Use Zustand for frontend state management
nodes.rationale: React Context + useReducer was verbose and Redux added too much boilerplate; Zustand offered a minimal selector-based API with no provider wrapping.

nodes.label: Store project memory inside repos, not a database
nodes.rationale: Other AI project managers store context in proprietary/cloud formats; LoopDeck needed to be local-first and repo-portable so context travels with the code — .loopdeck/ lives per-repo, the global registry is an index not source of truth.

nodes.label: Markdown for agent memory files (decisions.md, loops.md)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over YAML/JSON/SQLite because Markdown is human-readable, understood by all LLMs, and needs no parser library on the agent side; parsed with regex-free line-by-line scanning enforced by convention, not schema.

nodes.label: Sidebar tab navigation in ProjectDetail instead of single scroll view
nodes.rationale: V2 added Decisions and Loops tabs alongside Overview; a single scroll view would be too long, so tabs give clear separation of concerns via a left sidebar + right content panel.

nodes.label: Dual Stop hooks for agent memory auto-write (superseded)
nodes.rationale: A prompt-based hook (richer content) and a shell-script fallback (mechanical guarantee) were made complementary in settings.local.json's Stop hook.

nodes.label: Stop hook dirty-flag gating (temporary workaround)
nodes.rationale: The Stop hook fired on every session end, even pure Q&A, causing repetitive nags; a PreToolUse hook creates .claude/.session-dirty on Edit/Write and the Stop hook only reminds when the flag exists. Flagged as temporary — the real fix is moving agent control into the LoopDeck app itself.

nodes.label: Moved LoopDeck memory hooks to global config with .loopdeck/ gating
nodes.rationale: The memory-update hooks were project-local to the loopdeck repo; any LoopDeck-tracked project with a .loopdeck/ dir should get the same automation, so scripts moved to ~/.claude/hooks/ gated on .loopdeck/ existence and configured in global settings.json.

nodes.label: Fixed Stop hook matcher and dirty-flag race condition
nodes.rationale: matcher: "" only matched an empty string, never real stop reasons; changed to ".*". The Python hook also consumed .session-dirty (deleting it) starving the shell fallback; now only the shell fallback consumes the flag.

nodes.label: Git-age-based project status auto-classification
nodes.rationale: Project status should reflect reality, not manual input; rescan_project derives Active/Warning/NonActive from last-commit age (0-6/7-30/30+ days), falling back to last_modified with Archived remaining manual.

nodes.label: Stop hook must use command type, not prompt type
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's hook system only allows type: "prompt" on PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest, not Stop; the Stop hook was replaced with a type: "command" python3 script emitting hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext.

nodes.label: Adopt Tailwind CSS v4 + OKLCH dark palette from AI Project Command
nodes.rationale: LoopDeck's plain-CSS BEM/hex UI was replaced with the more polished reference app's Tailwind v4 + OKLCH design system, deleting all component CSS in favor of a single styles.css with design tokens and a sidebar-nav AppShell.

nodes.label: Per-content-block streaming granularity for ClaudeEvent
nodes.rationale: Chose to break each NDJSON assistant message into one ClaudeEvent per content block (TextDelta/ThinkingDelta) rather than one event per line, giving the frontend natural render-ready granularity while ResponseAccumulator still ingests the full message per call.

nodes.label: Separate batch and streaming send_message paths (not refactored into one)
nodes.rationale: Refactoring send_message to reuse send_message_streaming with a dropped channel was rejected; the two paths share ResponseAccumulator but differ enough (~15 lines of duplication) that keeping them separate is cheaper than the abstraction.

nodes.label: Best-effort channel sends in streaming (closed channel is not an error)
nodes.rationale: If the frontend closes the Tauri Channel<ClaudeEvent> mid-turn, sends are dropped silently (let _ = channel.send(...)) rather than aborting the turn, since the transcript is always recorded after the turn completes regardless.

nodes.label: Stop hook re-injection caused runaway token usage (~30M/hr)
nodes.rationale: The Stop hook instructed the model to read loops.md/decisions.md after every turn, re-injecting on every wake-up; with the files grown to ~35K tokens combined, each turn paid ~38K tokens, consuming ~30M tokens in under an hour. Fixed by an append-only ~3-line nudge, a missing PreToolUse dirty-flag hook, and archiving loops.md History (1541→118 lines).

nodes.label: Streaming command returns () not AgentResponse
nodes.rationale: Returning AgentResponse alongside the streaming Channel would create two sources of truth; the terminal ClaudeEvent::Result on the channel carries the full aggregated response instead.

nodes.label: Frontend streaming chat UI uses Channel events as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: The invoke Promise is used only for infra-level error catching; model-level errors surface from the ClaudeEvent::Result event, consistent with streaming commands returning ().

nodes.label: Streaming "Start next loop" variant added for UI consistency
nodes.rationale: agent_start_loop_streaming mirrors the batch agent_start_loop's prompt-building exactly, avoiding duplicating build_next_loop_prompt on the frontend, so the first turn of a session also streams like follow-ups.

nodes.label: Extracted presentational Chat component from AgentPanel
nodes.rationale: Chat.tsx became a pure presentational component with zero Tauri/Channel imports, driven entirely by props/callbacks, so it is reusable and testable while AgentPanel retains sole ownership of the Channel lifecycle.

nodes.label: Agent Runner uses terminal theme, not Chat bubbles
nodes.rationale: The standalone Agent Runner was meant to feel like a developer tool (tmux-for-AI-agents), so it renders its own monospace terminal output rather than reusing Chat's bubble UI, though it reuses the same streaming orchestration pattern.

nodes.label: Activity Feed merges all sources into single chronological timeline
nodes.rationale: A single merged ActivityEvent[] discriminated by kind avoids fragmenting chronology across per-source sections; date-only sources get synthesized midnight-UTC timestamps to sort correctly.

nodes.label: Standalone Decisions + Loops use expand-in-place cards, not detail pages
nodes.rationale: With TanStack Router not yet adopted, navigating to per-item detail pages would add routing-like state management prematurely; expand-in-place keeps the list visible for context.

nodes.label: TanStack Router: memory history, Zustand for data only
nodes.rationale: Adopted @tanstack/react-router with createMemoryHistory (no browser URL bar in Tauri); Zustand retains data state but no longer owns the current view, reducing the persisted slice to {selectedProject, detailTab}.

nodes.label: Spec layer in docs/epics/, runtime layer in .loopdeck/
nodes.rationale: Planning past ~10 flat loops.md items broke down; putting epics directly in .loopdeck/epics.md would conflate authored plan with runtime state. Epics/PRDs live under docs/epics/<slug>/ (git-tracked), bridged to .loopdeck/loops.md by a single promote-to-loop action; the agent stays unaware of the hierarchy.

nodes.label: YAML frontmatter for spec files, bullets for runtime files
nodes.rationale: Epics need to be indexed (grouped by milestone, filtered by status), so spec-layer files carry YAML frontmatter (structured, queryable) while runtime-layer .loopdeck/*.md files keep the lenient **Field**: value bullet convention agents write.

nodes.label: Split loopdeck-orchestrator into runner + author + memory
nodes.rationale: With the spec layer moved to docs/epics/, the fat orchestrator's re-decomposition strategy collided with the app-owned plan; split into loopdeck-loop-runner (mechanics), loopdeck-epic-author (on-demand drafting aid), and loopdeck-memory (write conventions) to avoid recreating autonomous-planning drift.

nodes.label: Managed-skills refresh via version manifest
nodes.rationale: copy_skills skips any skill whose SKILL.md already exists, making the orchestrator split unreachable on existing projects; a .claude/skills/.loopdeck-manifest.json now records installed skills + app version, so the loopdeck-prefixed app-managed skills refresh on version bump while user-owned skills are untouched.

nodes.label: Auth token stored in OS keychain, not config.yaml
nodes.rationale: The threat model is local exposure (backups, cloud-sync, accidental commits), not a remote attacker; the token moved into the OS credential store via the keyring crate, resolved into a local AgentConfig only at spawn time. (Later reverted to a 0600 plaintext file per SECURITY.md T5 because unsigned builds re-prompted for the keychain password on every spawn.)

nodes.label: Offload blocking I/O in Tauri commands to spawn_blocking
nodes.rationale: scan_directory, import_project, list_projects, and rescan_project ran walkdir + git subprocess spawns directly on the tokio worker, stalling every other IPC command; moved to tokio::task::spawn_blocking with the Mutex<GlobalConfig> lock no longer held across the I/O.

nodes.label: Reap claude child off the tokio worker in Drop via spawn_blocking
nodes.rationale: ClaudeSession::drop's synchronous poll_reap could sleep up to 7s on a tokio worker thread since Drop can't .await; child became Option<Child> so Drop can detach the graceful-then-forceful reap onto the blocking pool via a fire-and-forget spawn_blocking, with a synchronous fallback when no runtime is attached.

nodes.label: Resolve claude/git to absolute, vetted paths at spawn
nodes.rationale: Both subprocess spawns handed a bare name to OS PATH search, resolvable against a hostile project's cwd; a new binary module skips non-absolute $PATH entries, vets the executable bit, and pins the result in a OnceLock for the process lifetime.

nodes.label: Phase 3b — Bounded untrusted work (FR4)
nodes.rationale: Closes Gate A item 6; a new limits.rs centralizes named budgets (SCAN_MAX_*, SEARCH_MAX_*, README/SPEC/SKILL/TRANSCRIPT_MAX_BYTES, STREAM_LINE_MAX_BYTES, ACCUMULATOR_MAX_*, PARKED_SLOT_TIMEOUT) so every untrusted-input surface (scan, search walk, file reads, NDJSON stream lines, ResponseAccumulator, parked approvals) stops-and-returns-partial or errors with AppError::Limit instead of freezing the UI or exhausting memory.

nodes.label: Phase 3a — Central registered-project boundary (FR3)
nodes.rationale: Closes Gate A item 5; a new paths.rs module (canonical_root, resolve_registered_root, resolve_within, canonicalize_prefix) becomes the single chokepoint every project-scoped command funnels through, closing a toggle_prd_loop traversal bug and an unchecked agent_add_allow_rule write.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Crash-safe critical state + recoverable registry
nodes.rationale: Closes Gate A items 3-4; a hand-rolled persist.rs atomic_write (temp-file + fsync + same-dir rename) replaces every truncate-then-write, and GlobalConfig::load_from_path gets a 4-step recovery (primary/backup/malformed) so a corrupted registry is never silently overwritten with an empty default.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Honest permission contract (ConfirmChanges default)
nodes.rationale: Closes Gate A item 1; fixed four contradictions where --permission-mode acceptEdits, a broad curated .claude/settings.json allowlist, misleadingly-named PolicyDefault types, and a missing UI indicator together silently auto-approved all file edits and most build/test execution despite the UI implying gating. PolicyDefault renamed to PermissionMode (Allow→ConfirmChanges); AutonomousProject deliberately deferred as YAGNI.

nodes.label: Transient gateway-error retry for agent turns (retry.rs)
nodes.rationale: A transient 529-overloaded gateway response arrived as a normal Ok(AgentResponse{is_error:true}), ending the loop on one blip; retry.rs adds a substring-matched is_overloaded check, exponential backoff (~2s/4s/8s, MAX_ATTEMPTS=4), and a streaming ClaudeEvent::Retrying event, while keeping transcript recording outside the retry loop so a retried turn appears as one exchange.

nodes.label: Panic/abort audit + hardening (P2 robustness)
nodes.rationale: Under panic = "abort", any reachable unwrap()/expect() is a full process-abort defect; a crate-wide grep classified every production panic site, fixing skills.rs's user-input-reachable .expect("hook event must be an array") via lenient coercion and hardening lib.rs's startup .expect() to a logged exit(1).

nodes.label: Top-level React error boundary (P2 robustness)
nodes.rationale: A render-time crash anywhere outside the router's errorComponent blanked the window; a self-contained RootErrorBoundary class component (no Tauri/router/theme imports) wraps <App> with Reload-app and Try-again (keyed remount) recovery options.

nodes.label: Loop record — Absolute, vetted binary resolution for claude + git (P2 security)
nodes.rationale: Same fix as the corresponding decisions.md entry: binary.rs resolve_command() walks $PATH, skips non-absolute components, vets executability, and pins the result in a OnceLock; git() is invoked via git -C <repo> instead of current_dir + bare name.

nodes.label: Loop record — ClaudeSession::drop reap moved off the tokio worker (P2 robustness)
nodes.rationale: Implementation record matching the corresponding decisions.md entry: child: Child became Option<Child> so Drop can detach the bounded graceful-then-forceful reap onto spawn_blocking, preserving the 5s-EOF-then-2s-SIGKILL sequence.

nodes.label: Loop record — Blocking I/O offloaded to spawn_blocking (P2 robustness)
nodes.rationale: Implementation record matching the corresponding decisions.md entry: scan_directory/import_project/list_projects/rescan_project's walkdir + git spawns moved into spawn_blocking with the config lock held only briefly around the I/O.

nodes.label: Loop record — Auth token moved to OS keychain (P2 secret hygiene)
nodes.rationale: Implementation record matching the corresponding decisions.md entry: secrets.rs load/store/delete_auth_token over the keyring crate; the plaintext token never crosses IPC to the renderer, only a has_auth_token presence flag does.

PRD — Global Agent Configuration (overview)
AgentConfig struct (auth_token, base_url, model, effort) in global config.yaml
Design rationale: global-first agent config, per-project later
nodes.rationale: Most developers use one API key and one provider; per-project model overrides are an edge case (YAGNI). Matches tools like GitHub Copilot/Cursor — global settings with per-workspace overrides as a future advanced feature.

nodes.label: Issue 1 — Bash tool calls stall under the loopdeck-spawned claude process (no TTY)
nodes.rationale: A spawned, piped-stdin/stdout claude process has no TTY to satisfy a Bash approval prompt, so any control_request hangs until SEND_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT (180s); confirmed by comparing sdk-cli vs. interactive-cli transcripts of the identical git add command.

nodes.label: Issue 3 — Persisted turns don't render tool calls / thinking (TurnBubble)
nodes.rationale: StreamingBubble renders tool_calls/thinking live, but the persisted TurnBubble in Chat.tsx renders only turn.text, even though both fields are populated on ConversationTurn — fix is to render them unconditionally (no !isComplete gate) since they're history.

nodes.label: Permission-mode option matrix (default / acceptEdits / auto / bypassPermissions)
acceptEdits does not unblock Bash execution (only covers Edit/Write/NotebookEdit)
nodes.rationale: The accompanying code comment claimed acceptEdits 'keeps Bash guardrails intact while unblocking the autonomous loop' — verified false via claude --help: acceptEdits auto-approves only Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, so every orchestrator loop full of git/cargo/npm Bash calls still stalls on the first command.

nodes.label: PRD — Multi-Project Claude Sessions (overview)
Two-layer lock concurrency model (outer std::sync::Mutex map + inner per-project tokio::sync::Mutex)
Conversation persistence to .loopdeck/sessions/active.jsonl + archive-<ts>.jsonl
Start always begins fresh; Send resumes the live/last session (--resume only on Send)
nodes.rationale: Start (try_lock, reject if busy) always drops any live session, archives the transcript, and spawns fresh without --resume so context re-seeds from .loopdeck/ memory; Send (lock().await, queues) continues the live process and re-spawns with --resume only after an app restart, so no turn is ever force-interrupted.
